subject: Console privacy takeaway + customer QA sheet
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Console privacy takeaway + customer QA sheet

Team —

Thanks for jumping on this quickly. Legal got a note from Acme (they're evaluating Hosted API for a multi-region deployment) asking for copy we can surface in the Console: a short, public-facing paragraph about data handling (hosted API), a one-line explanation about subprocessors & why we list them, and a Q&A with 3–4 canned answers they can copy into their procurement packet. They specifically called out cross-border transfers and the subprocessor list cadence.

I've attached a first-pass doc with snippets and a subprocessor map export. Ask: can you review the three areas below and return edits/alternatives by EOD tomorrow?

1) Console short paragraph (30–60 words) for the product settings page explaining what data we persist, retention default, and how customers can opt for stricter settings.
2) Subprocessor one-liner (sales-facing / non-legal) — explain why we publish a list and how often it updates.
3) Quick Q&A (4 items) — short, copyable answers for procurement (SOC2 evidence, DPA signature, data location controls, and cross-border safeguard).

I've attached: console_privacy_snippets_v1.docx, subprocessor_map_2027-07.xlsx, customer_faq_shortlist.pdf.

Notes: keep language plain; avoid full legal citations in the product UI. We can link to the full DPA from the Console.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Console privacy takeaway + customer QA sheet

Kim — thanks, saw the doc. High-level suggestions:

- Console paragraph: make it actionable and UI-consumable. Proposed copy (38 words): “Redwood stores short-lived request data to serve your application and improve performance. You can set a retention policy per-project; enable strict retention to auto-delete logs after X days. See full data handling terms in the DPA.”

- Subprocessor one-liner (sales tone): "We publish the list of subprocessors to be transparent about who processes request data on our behalf; we update the list when we add providers and notify customers in-app."

- Q&A: I trimmed some longer answers to single sentences and added a link to the subprocessor export. Questions to confirm: do we want to state update cadence as "weekly" or "when changes occur + 30-day notice"?

Priyom — any constraints from the Console UX (character limits, modal vs. tooltip) we should align on? Laura — I've included a version that is a little more sales-friendly; you can swap words to match our buyer-facing playbook.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior PM, Redwood Console

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Console privacy takeaway + customer QA sheet

Thanks Marcus — good direction. From Sales POV: keep two variants — "Plain" and "Legal-lite". Plain to show in the UI, Legal-lite for the linked modal. My edits:

- Plain (short): "We store request data briefly to respond to API calls. You can set stricter retention policies in Project settings. We publish our subprocessors and notify customers about important changes."

- Legal-lite (modal headline): "Data handling & subprocessors — quick summary" followed by 2–3 bullet lines and a link to the DPA and subprocessor map.

Q&A suggestions (copyable):
• "Where can I get SOC 2 evidence?" — "Contact your account team; we provide a SOC 2 checklist after an NDA."
• "How often does the subprocessor list change?" — "We publish updates when a new subprocessor is added; customers with active contracts receive notice 30 days before the change."
• "Will my data leave the region?" — "By default requests are processed in the region you choose; in limited cases we may route to additional regions for availability. See the DPA for details."

Priyom — can you vet the underlined operational statements (SOC2 delivery flow, 30-day notice) so we don't commit something we don't follow operationally?

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, GTM Operations

Hi Sara / Acme team —

Following up with a short set of snippets we've prepared for the Console and for procurement. Below is the "Plain" copy we intend to show in the Product Settings page, plus three short Q&A items. Happy to adjust wording — would you prefer us to include a direct link to the full subprocessor spreadsheet or to a downloadable PDF?

Console plain copy (product settings)
"We store request data briefly to serve your application and improve performance. You can set stricter retention settings per project. We publish our subprocessors and notify customers about material changes."

Customer Q&A (copyable)
1) Where can I get SOC 2 evidence? — "Contact your account team; we provide SOC 2 documentation under NDA."
2) How often does the subprocessor list change? — "We publish updates when a new subprocessor is added and provide 30 days' notice to impacted customers."
3) Will my data leave the region? — "Requests are processed in the chosen region by default. In rare availability scenarios we may route to nearby regions; see the DPA for cross-border safeguards."

Attachments: console_privacy_snippets_v1.docx (editable), subprocessor_map_2027-07.xlsx (export), customer_faq_shortlist.pdf

Please reply with any edits or preferences — we can update the modal copy or provide an expanded FAQ for procurement if you want.

Best,
Kim
